app.tagline: Remote control for your robot hub
hint.start: Turn the hub on and close other apps that are connected to it. If the hub is not in the list, press the Bluetooth button on the hub.
hint.choose: Pick your hub in the browser window.
hint.upload: Sending the control program to slot {0}.
hint.ready: Ready to drive. If the connection drops, the robot stops by itself.
hint.nochoice: No hub selected. If the hub is not listed, press its Bluetooth button and close other apps that are connected to it.
hint.fail: Could not connect. Is Bluetooth on? Restart the hub, close other apps that are connected to it and try again.
hint.stopped: The program on the hub has stopped. Tap Start program to keep driving.
hint.reconnectFail: Reconnecting failed. Is the hub still on? Tap Connect to hub.
keys.note:
WASD or arrows: drive
Shift: turbo · H: horn
Space: stop
horn.title: Horn (H)
mode.tank: Tank: two sliders, one per motor
mode.tilt: Tilt: steer by tilting the device
tilt.denied: No access to the motion sensor of this device.
tilt.none: This device does not report tilt data.
set.name: Name
robots.title: Build a robot
robots.help: Build a robot with the free building instructions from LEGO® Education, then tap Use: the app sets the ports and puts example programs in Code.
ldr.title: Designed it yourself in BrickLink Studio?
ldr.help: Export your model from Studio as an LDraw™ file (.ldr or .mpd, the file format of www.ldraw.org) and open it here. The app finds the hub, motors and sensors and suggests a profile. Cables are not in such a file: check the ports with the diagram once the hub is connected.
build.title: Building guide
build.rover: Example: Rover (only parts from the SPIKE™ Prime set)
build.veegbot: Example: sweeper robot with a turning arm, colour and force sensor (all motors of the SPIKE™ Prime set)
build.fail: The building guide could not be opened: {0}
build.offline: Building guides work from the website (online the first time), not as a single file.
build.auto: This file had no building steps; the app made them itself, from the bottom up.
build.missing: {0} kind(s) of parts are not in the brick set and show as a grey block.
build.help: Drag to turn, pinch to zoom. The new parts of this step have their real colour; what you already built is lighter.
build.saved: The building guide now belongs to profile "{0}".
build.noRoom: The building guide is too large to keep; you can still look at it now.
build.none: This profile has no building guide yet.

ldr.io: This is a Studio project file (.io). Export it from Studio as an LDraw file (.ldr) and open that.
ldr.bad: I cannot read this file as an LDraw model.
ldr.none: No SPIKE™ hub, motors or sensors found in "{0}" ({1} parts).
ldr.like: This looks like the {0}: the ports come from its building instructions.

ldr.noHub: No hub in the file; assuming a {0}.
ldr.notPlaced: {0} part(s) no longer fit in the profile.
ldr.noDrive: No two matching motors found to drive with.
ldr.otherHubNote: It contains another Powered Up hub; BrickHubRemote only works with the SPIKE™ hubs.
ldr.made: Profile "{0}" made. Connect the hub and see whether the diagram turns green.
robots.note: The building instructions belong to LEGO® Education and open on their website. BrickHubRemote is not a product of the LEGO Group.
robots.used: Profile "{0}" is ready, with example programs in Code.
robots.wrongHub: This model is for the {0}; your hub does not have those ports.
model.db.name: Driving Base 1 and 2
model.db.desc: Drives on motors C and D. Motor E at the front powers the lift arm or dozer blade from Driving Base 2.
model.db3.name: Driving Base 3
model.db3.desc: The driving base with a colour sensor on B looking down: stop on a line or a colour.
model.adb.name: Advanced Driving Base
model.adb.desc: Large motors on A and E to drive, motors C and D for tools, colour sensors on B and F. Driving the wrong way round? Swap left and right under Drive.
model.ess.name: Car with two motors
model.ess.desc: Any SPIKE™ Essential model that drives on two motors: left on A, right on B. A wheel turning the wrong way? Switch reverse on or off under Drive.
wire.title: How to connect it
wire.live: Green: the hub sees it. Red: nothing found on that port. Grey: found, but not in this profile.
py.x.line: Drive until the colour sensor on {0} sees black
set.samePort: Left and right are set to the same port.
set.driveHelp: Tap Test: the wheel should briefly turn forward. If it turns backward, switch Reverse on. If the robot pulls to the right, move the trim towards L.
aux.title: Extra motors
aux.name: Name
aux.toggle: On/off: tap to start and stop
aux.gripHelp: Use Minus and Plus to close the gripper, then tap Closed is here. Travel is how far it opens.
sens.title: Sensors
sens.help: Works with a distance sensor that faces forward. The robot will not drive further forward within the stop distance; reversing and turning still work. The reading arrives with a small delay, so pick a larger distance at high speed.
app.title: App
app.slotHelp: The program in the selected slot is overwritten when you connect.
hub.title: Hub
hub.name: Name
about.title: About
about.text: BrickHubRemote is an independent project. It works with the LEGO® Education SPIKE™ Prime and SPIKE™ Essential hubs on their standard firmware. LEGO® and SPIKE™ are trademarks of the LEGO Group, which does not sponsor, authorize or endorse this app. The communication protocol is publicly documented by the LEGO Group under the Apache License 2.0.

share.offline: This page was opened locally. The link only works on other devices once the app is online.
share.bad: The shared link is not valid.

msg.slotLater: The new slot applies after reconnecting.

err.noStart: The hub cannot start the program
play.hub: Connected: you hear it on the hub.
play.phone: Not connected: you hear it on this device. Connect to play it on the hub.
move.title: Move
move.help: Dances and routes drive in the Drive screen. STOP, the space bar or the joystick takes over at once.
move.empty: No route yet. Choose Record a route first.
move.short: Nothing recorded: drive a little first.
music.title: Songs
talk.title: Robot talk
talk.help: When connecting, at an obstacle and when the battery runs low.
speak.title: Robot language
speak.ph: Type what the robot should say
speak.help: The hub says your sentence itself in robot beeps, with a moving mouth on the light matrix. A question goes up at the end.
anim.title: Animation
anim.help: Tap a picture to draw it. Play shows the pictures one after another on the hub's light matrix until you tap Stop.
anim.noScreen: This hub has no light matrix.
pyv.title: Your blocks as Python
pyv.help: This is your program as MicroPython for the hub. Open it in the Python editor to change it and run it on the hub itself.
pyv.noCopy: Copying does not work here; select the text yourself.
pyv.full: You already have 30 Python programs. Delete one first.
pyg.title: Made from the blocks of "{0}" in BrickHubRemote.
pyg.note: Helper functions are at the top; your own program is at the bottom.
pyg.ports: Ports from your robot profile; change them here if your robot is wired differently.
pyg.flip: -1 = this motor turns the other way
pyg.program: Your program: every stack of blocks is a function of its own
pyg.main: Start all stacks at the same time
pyg.empty: There are no blocks with a start block yet.
pyg.stopMode: (set the stop mode of motor {0} to {1}: use motor.stop(port.{0}, stop=...))
pyg.orient: (turning the light matrix: not in Python yet)
pyg.btnLight: (colour of the button light: not in Python yet)
pyg.songStart: (in Python the song plays to the end before going on)
pyg.stopOthers: (stopping the other stacks: not in Python yet)
phrase.2: Out of my way, here I come!
phrase.3: I am hungry. Do you have a battery for me?
piano.title: Piano
piano.recording: Recording: play your song on the piano.
dbg.retry: The connection dropped while connecting, retry {0}.
dbg.lost: The hub closed the connection (last step: {0}).
code.noImu: The hub sends no motion sensor data: turn skipped.
code.imgHelp: Tap a light to turn it on or off.
code.help: Drag blocks from the list and snap them together. Every program starts with a When block. Run makes the robot follow it; STOP or another screen stops everything.
py.help: Real MicroPython running on the hub, with the same commands as the Python of the official SPIKE™ app. Run puts your code in slot {0} (the remote control stays in slot {1}) and print() appears in the output. STOP or another screen stops your program. If the connection drops it keeps running: then stop it with the button on the hub.
py.cheat: Cheat sheet: Python on the hub
py.exConfirm: Replace your code with the example "{0}"?
py.running: Python is running on the hub. STOP stops it.
py.error: Error in your code on line {0}
py.lost: Connection lost while Python was running. Is the robot still moving? Press the button on the hub.
py.x.hello: Say hello with light and sound
py.x.pair: Two motors as a driving pair: left {0}, right {1}
py.x.side: Straight on, then a quarter turn
py.x.wall: Drive until the distance sensor on {0} sees something within 10 cm
py.x.tilt: Show how the hub is tilted, 20 times
py.c.main: your program; await waits until something is done
py.c.deg: one turn, and wait until it is done
code.noHat: Put a When block at the top of your program, for example "When the program starts".
play.small: The SPIKE™ Essential hub has no speaker or light matrix: you hear it on this device.
